mainTopic: When a מוקצה object becomes usable on שבת through attachment, placement, or an action (stone on a barrel, branches, building stones), and the window-shutter dispute about adding to a temporary tent
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה: a branch tied to a pitcher may be used to draw water, and רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about a window shutter. The גמרא then discusses a stone sitting on a barrel. רבי יוחנן's ruling comes in two versions. In רבה's version, a stone placed there on purpose makes the barrel a בסיס לדבר האסור. In רב יוסף's version, it becomes a כיסוי for the barrel. Each version is tested against a משנה about a stone in a gourd. The dispute is explained as whether a physical מעשה is needed to make an object usable. This ties into a story about רבי and some building stones, where רבי אמי and רבי אסי each follow their own reasoning. Next, the גמרא asks whether the tied-branch rule contradicts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רב ששת and רב אשי each answer. Finally, רבי יוחנן explains that the shutter dispute is only about adding to an existing אהל עראי, and the גמרא begins to explain 'בין כך ובין כך', with the answer continuing on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A branch tied to a pitcher may be used to draw water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a vine branch tied to a pitcher may be used to fill water on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vine branch that is tied to a pitcher: one may fill water with it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the previous rule in the משנה. It says that a branch tied to a pitcher may be used on שבת to draw water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loose branch is normally מוקצה because it is not a כלי. Once it is tied to the pitcher, it works as the pitcher's handle or rope. That makes it part of the כלי, so using it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A vine branch
A pitcher or jug
One may fill (draw water)
An item set aside from use on שבת, which may not be moved

phrases.english: A vine branch that is tied to a pitcher —
one may fill water with it on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Tying it makes the branch part of the vessel.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A branch attached to a כלי becomes part of the כלי and may be used on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר on the window shutter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says a window shutter may be used only if it is tied to the window and hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a window shutter, רבי אליעזר says: when it is tied and hanging, one may close the window with it; if not, one may not close the window with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new case, a board used to close a window. רבי אליעזר allows using it only if it is attached and hanging from the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the shutter is tied on and hanging, it is clearly part of the window, so closing the window with it is not like building. If it is not attached, putting it in place looks like adding to the building, so he forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: A window shutter or plug
Tied and hanging
One may close or plug the opening
And if not

phrases.english: A window shutter,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
when it is tied and hanging —
one may shutter the window with it,
and if not — one may not shutter with it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a shutter may be used only when it is tied and hanging.

steps.title: The Sages permit the shutter either way
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר and allow using the shutter in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: in both this case and that case, one may close the window with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposing opinion. They allow using the shutter whether it is tied or not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, closing a window with a shutter is not building at all. So whether it is attached makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority opinion)
Either way; in both cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר requires the shutter to be tied and hanging. The חכמים permit it in all cases.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ — פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: both in this case and in that case — one may shutter with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי אליעזר's restriction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the shutter may be used whether or not it is tied.

steps.title: A stone resting on a barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: to remove a stone from a barrel, one tilts the barrel so the stone falls off.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned there in a משנה: a stone that is on top of a barrel — one tilts the barrel on its side and the stone falls off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a different משנה about a stone sitting on a barrel. This is a setup line: the next steps will explain when this rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone is מוקצה, so it may not be lifted directly by hand. The barrel itself may be moved, so one tilts it and lets the stone slide off. This indirect method lets a person reach the barrel's contents.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
We learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
A barrel
He tilts it on its side

steps.confusionAlert: This stone case comes from a different משנה, not from our משנה. The גמרא brings it up to discuss the general idea of objects becoming part of, or attached to, a כלי.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned in a mishna there:
A stone that is atop a barrel —
he tilts the barrel on its side, and the stone falls.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה stone on a barrel may be removed indirectly by tilting the barrel.

steps.title: רבה's version: a placed stone makes the barrel a base
steps.stepSummary: In רבה's report, רבי יוחנן limits the משנה to a forgotten stone. If the stone was placed on purpose, the barrel becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי אמי in the name of רבי יוחנן: they taught this only when one forgot the stone there. But when one placed it there, the barrel becomes a base for a forbidden object.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the משנה so that it applies only to a stone that was forgotten on the barrel. For a stone placed there deliberately, the barrel becomes a base for מוקצה and may not even be tilted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one deliberately placed the stone before שבת, the barrel was set up as the stone's holder. That makes the barrel a בסיס, which is itself forbidden to move. A forgotten stone does not have this effect.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only (in a limited case)
One who forgets
One who places on purpose
A base for a forbidden (מוקצה) object, which becomes forbidden too

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They only taught this where one forgets the stone there;
however, where one places it intentionally —
the barrel becomes a base for a prohibited object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the quoted משנה to a specific case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deliberately placed stone makes the barrel a בסיס, so the barrel may not be moved.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: a placed stone becomes a barrel cover
steps.stepSummary: In רב יוסף's report, רבי יוחנן also limits the משנה to a forgotten stone. But a placed stone becomes a כיסוי, so the case is more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: they taught this only when one forgot the stone there. But when one placed it there, it becomes a cover for the barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, opposite version of רבי יוחנן's statement. Here, placing the stone on purpose turns it into the barrel's lid, which may be handled like any lid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the משנה is talking about a forgotten stone. In רבה's version, deliberate placement makes things stricter (a בסיס). In רב יוסף's version, it makes things more lenient: the stone is designated as a lid and is no longer מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cover for the barrel
It becomes

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement. For a placed stone, רבה says the barrel becomes a בסיס (forbidden), and רב יוסף says the stone becomes a כיסוי (permitted).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They only taught this where one forgets it;
however, where one places it —
it becomes a cover for the barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רבי יוחנן's statement in the מניח case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deliberately placed stone becomes a כיסוי, so it is permitted to handle.

steps.title: רבה's challenge from a stone in a gourd
steps.stepSummary: רבה raises a difficulty from a משנה: a stone in a gourd used for drawing water may be used if it does not fall out. This suggests that a stone set in place for a purpose is not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: we raise an objection to our teaching. A stone that is in a gourd: if one fills water with it and the stone does not fall out, one may fill water with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה questions the version that treats a placed stone as making its holder a בסיס. He brings a case where a stone placed in a gourd is simply allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People put a stone in a gourd to weigh it down so it sinks. If the stone stays in while filling, the gourd may be used, which shows the stone became part of the כלי. That seems to contradict the idea that deliberately placing a stone makes its holder a forbidden בסיס.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise an objection to our teaching
A hollow gourd used for drawing water
And it does not fall out

phrases.english: Rabba said: We raise an objection to our halakha:
A stone that is in a gourd
if they fill with it and it does not fall —
one may fill with it!
phrases.notes: Implies that a stone designated for a purpose is no longer מוקצה.

steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a deliberately placed stone makes its holder a בסיס לדבר האסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the gourd case, a deliberately placed stone becomes part of the כלי and is permitted. So a placed stone should not make the barrel a forbidden base.

steps.title: The gourd case is different: the stone became a wall
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. The stone in the gourd was wedged in tightly and became part of the gourd's wall, unlike a stone just resting on a barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, since one wedged it in tightly, he made it into a wall of the gourd.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is pushed off by showing that the two cases are not comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone in the gourd is pressed in firmly and becomes a physical part of the כלי, like one of its walls. A stone merely resting on top of a barrel is not part of the barrel. So the gourd case proves nothing about the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (the comparison fails)
He wedged or fastened it tightly
He made it a wall (of the vessel)

steps.whatToRemember: A stone fastened into a כלי becomes part of the כלי itself. That is why the gourd case cannot challenge the barrel case.

phrases.english: And that is not so.
There, since he fastened it tightly —
he made it a wall of the gourd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the gourd stone and the barrel stone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gourd stone is fastened in and becomes a wall of the כלי, while the barrel stone merely rests on top.

steps.title: רב יוסף raises a difficulty against his own teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges his own version of the ruling from the end of the gourd משנה: if the stone falls out, one may not draw water with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We can raise a difficulty against our teaching. The משנה says that if the stone does not stay in, one may not draw water with the gourd.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף now turns the gourd משנה against himself. The end of that משנה seems to say that a stone that was set in place but is not firmly attached is still מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף holds that a stone placed on a barrel on purpose becomes a כיסוי, a usable cover, without any further action. But the gourd משנה says that if the stone falls out, the gourd may not be used, so the stone is treated as מוקצה. This suggests that placing a stone is not enough to make it a usable item.

keyTerms.meaning: and we raise a difficulty
our teaching (the ruling under discussion)
if not (if the stone does not stay in place)
draw or fill water

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב יוסף is challenging his OWN view. In step 7, רבה used the first part of the same משנה against his own view. Each scholar now uses a different part of the gourd משנה against himself.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: And we can raise a difficulty against our teaching:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is objecting to his own report of רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: If not (if the stone falls out), one may not draw water with it!
phrases.notes: The end of the gourd משנה. A stone that is not firmly attached seems to stay מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 7. רבה challenged his own view from the first part of the gourd משנה, and now רב יוסף challenges his own view from its last part.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's report that a stone placed on purpose becomes a כיסוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If placing a stone made it usable, then a loose stone in the gourd should also be usable. Yet the משנה forbids drawing water when the stone falls out.

steps.title: The gourd case is different because the stone was not secured
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. In the gourd, the person did not secure the stone, so he showed he did not treat it as part of the gourd.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not correct. There, since he did not wedge it in tightly, he showed that he does not treat it as part of the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects his own challenge. He explains why the loose gourd stone is different from a stone placed on a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a gourd, a stone only works as a weight if it is wedged in tightly. Leaving it loose shows the person never really made it part of the gourd. On a barrel, simply placing the stone on top is how a cover is normally used, so placement alone can make it a כיסוי.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so (the challenge fails)
he wedged or fastened it tightly
he actually set it aside (he did not treat it as part of the vessel)

phrases.english: But that is not so.
phrases.notes: The comparison is rejected.

phrases.english: There, since he did not wedge it in tightly,
phrases.notes: The gourd case.

phrases.english: he showed that he set it aside from being part of the vessel.
phrases.notes: Leaving it loose shows he never made it part of the gourd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9 by showing that the gourd case and the barrel case are not alike.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between a loose stone in a gourd and a stone placed on a barrel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In a gourd, the normal way to make a stone part of it is to wedge it in. A loose stone shows no such intent. On a barrel, simply resting a stone on top is the normal way to use a cover.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבה and רב יוסף actually disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses and asks for the underlying principle behind the two reports. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports agree about a forgotten stone. They differ only about a stone placed on purpose. The גמרא wants to name the exact legal idea that divides them.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: Asks for the underlying principle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both challenges are answered, the גמרא steps back to define the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that separates רבה and רב יוסף

steps.title: Is a physical action needed or not?
steps.stepSummary: רבה holds that a real action (מעשה) is needed to make a stone a usable item. רב יוסף holds that no action is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (רבה) holds that we require an action, and the other master (רב יוסף) holds that we do not require an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The dispute is whether turning a stone into a usable item needs a physical action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, placing a stone on a barrel is not enough to make it a cover. The stone stays מוקצה and makes the barrel a בסיס. For רב יוסף, placing it with intent is enough to make it a כיסוי. This explains both earlier positions.

keyTerms.meaning: one master holds
we require
a physical action (to change the item's status)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה needs a מעשה to make a stone usable, so a placed stone stays מוקצה. רב יוסף does not need a מעשה, so a stone placed with intent becomes a כיסוי.

phrases.english: One master holds that we require an action,
phrases.notes: רבה.

phrases.english: and the other master holds that we do not require an action.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether a physical action is required to remove a stone's מוקצה status

steps.title: The same dispute in a story about רבי and building stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this dispute already existed. רבי חנינא reports that רבי told his students only to designate the stones in their minds for sitting on שבת, with no action required.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning. When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי חנינא (and some say רבי זירא said in the name of רבי חנינא): Once רבי went to a certain place and found a row of building stones. He told his students: Go out and designate them in your minds so that we can sit on them tomorrow. And רבי did not require them to do any action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who passed on the two versions of רבי יוחנן's statement, are each following their own line of reasoning. To show this, it brings a story about רבי and building stones. In רבי חנינא's version of the story, thought alone was enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building stones are normally מוקצה. In רבי חנינא's version, רבי required only thought (לחשב), with no physical action. This story is the background for the next steps. There, רבי אמי and רבי אסי, the sources of רבה and רב יוסף, each describe רבי's instruction in a way that fits their own view.

keyTerms.meaning: they follow their own reasoning
a row of building stones
and designate them in your minds (by intent)
he required them

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי אמי and רבי אסי, the transmitters behind רבה and רב יוסף. Each stays consistent with his own view elsewhere.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: as when Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael), he said that Rabbi Chanina said,
phrases.notes: Chain of transmission.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Chanina said:
phrases.notes: An alternate chain. The teaching itself is the same.

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: Once Rabbi went to a certain place
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and found a row of building stones,
phrases.notes: Building stones are normally מוקצה.

phrases.english: and he said to his students: Go out and designate them in your minds
phrases.notes: Designation by thought.

phrases.english: so that we can sit on them tomorrow (on Shabbat),
and Rabbi did not require them to do an action.
phrases.notes: Thought alone was enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the מעשה dispute from step 12 to an earlier disagreement about רבי's instruction.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אמי and רבי אסי are consistent with their own views (רבי אמי requires a significant action, רבי אסי accepts a minimal one)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי and the building stones. רבי חנינא's version says only thought was needed. Within רבי יוחנן's version, רבי אמי ('arrange them') and רבי אסי ('rub them') each describe רבי's instruction in a way that fits their own view (steps 14-16).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי did require an action
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the story differently. רבי did require his students to do a physical action to the stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי required them to do an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different version of the same story. In his version, thought alone was not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite version of the story: thought alone was not enough. רבי יוחנן is the source behind both רבי אמי and רבי אסי. Their disagreement about which action רבי required (step 16) is where the לטעמייהו parallel shows up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi required them to do an action.
phrases.notes: Thought alone was not sufficient.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הִצְרִיכָן רַבִּי לְמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing version of the story told in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי required a physical action to make the building stones usable on שבת.

steps.title: Which action did רבי require?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what action רבי told his students to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he say to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the details of רבי יוחנן's version. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an action was required, we need to know what kind. The answer will show how big an action is needed to change the stones' status.

keyTerms.meaning: what did he say to them?

phrases.english: What did he say to them?
phrases.notes: Which action did he require?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the action mentioned in step 14.

steps.title: Arrange the stones, or rub them clean
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says רבי told them to arrange the stones. רבי אסי says he told them to rub the stones clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: He told them, 'Go out and arrange them.' רבי אסי said: He told them, 'Go out and rub them clean.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers about which action רבי required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי says the students had to arrange the stones for sitting, which is a real, significant action. רבי אסי says it was enough to rub off the mortar, which is a minimal action. This is the 'לטעמייהו' from step 13. רבי אמי, the source of רבה's version, requires a real מעשה. רבי אסי, the source of רב יוסף's version, is satisfied with almost no action.

keyTerms.meaning: and arrange them (set them in order for sitting)
and rub them clean (scrape off dirt or mortar)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבי's instruction. In רבי חנינא's version, thought alone was enough. In רבי יוחנן's version, an action was needed. Within רבי יוחנן's version, רבי אמי says arranging the stones (a real מעשה), matching his stricter בסיס report through רבה. רבי אסי says only rubbing them (a minimal action), matching his more lenient כיסוי report through רב יוסף (steps 5-6).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
He told them, 'Go out and arrange them.'
phrases.notes: A more significant action.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
He told them, 'Go out and rub them clean.'
phrases.notes: A smaller action, such as scraping off mortar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either arranging the stones (רבי אמי) or rubbing them clean (רבי אסי)

steps.title: What Did רבי's Students Sit On?
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree about what material was in the story of רבי. רבי יוסי בן שאול says it was a stack of beams. רבי יוחנן בן שאול says it was a ship's sounding pole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוסי בן שאול said it was a stack of beams. רבי יוחנן בן שאול said it was the sounding pole of a ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new report about the story of רבי and his students. According to this report, the items were not stones at all. There are two opinions about what they really were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we assumed the students sat on stones. Now one view says they sat on a stack of beams, and the other says they sat on a ship's pole used to measure water depth. The type of item matters, because some items are valuable and their owner avoids using them for anything else.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a teaching or dispute of the אמוראים)
A stack of wooden beams
A ship's sounding pole, used to measure how deep the water is

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said:
It was a stack of beams.
phrases.notes: Not stones, as we had assumed until now.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul said:
It was the sounding pole of a ship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story of רבי and identifies the actual material involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The items in רבי's story were either a stack of beams (רבי יוסי בן שאול) or a ship's sounding pole (רבי יוחנן בן שאול).

steps.title: How the Two Views Relate
steps.stepSummary: Whoever says רבי allowed sitting on the ship's pole would certainly allow beams. Whoever says רבי allowed beams might forbid the pole, because its owner is careful with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said it was a sounding pole would all the more so allow beams. But the one who said it was beams would say that a sounding pole is different, because the owner is particular about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the two opinions relate to each other. One view is more lenient than the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ship's pole is more valuable, and its owner does not want it used for other things that could bend or damage it. So if רבי allowed even the pole, he would surely allow simple beams. But if the story was only about beams, the pole could still be forbidden as מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a 'surely' argument)
He is particular about it (does not want it used for other things)
Set aside from use because of fear of financial loss

steps.whatToRemember: The pole view is the more lenient one. It includes beams, but the beams view does not necessarily include the pole.

phrases.english: The one who said 'sounding pole'
would all the more so allow a stack of beams,
and the one who said 'stack of beams'
would say: but a sounding pole, one is particular about it.
phrases.notes: The owner worries it will warp, so it is set aside from other uses.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דַּאֲמַר גָּשׁוֹשׁ כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן סְוָאר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the dispute just quoted and shows which opinion is broader.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sounding-pole view includes beams. The beams view may still forbid the pole as מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.

steps.title: The משנה Requires a Tied Branch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a vine branch tied to a pitcher. It infers that only a tied branch is permitted, and an untied one is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a vine branch that is tied to a pitcher may be used to draw water. If it is tied, yes. If it is not tied, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and makes an inference from its wording. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically says the branch is 'tied.' The גמרא reads this as a condition: an untied branch may not be used. That suggests a piece of wood needs an action, tying, before it counts as a usable item on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A vine branch
Tied
Yes / no (used here to infer a rule from the wording)

phrases.english: A vine branch that is tied, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: it may be used to draw water with a pitcher.

phrases.english: Tied, yes, it is permitted;
not tied, no, it is not permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, linked to the earlier question of whether an action is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording, only a tied branch may be used, not an untied one.

steps.title: Does the משנה Disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who does not require tying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that our משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the משנה goes against a known תנא. The proof for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה requires tying, it seems to hold that wood needs an action to become usable. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that no action is needed. So the משנה would not fit his view, and the גמרא would rather not leave it that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא usually tries to avoid)
A תנא who holds that tying is not needed

phrases.english: Shall we say that our משנה
is not in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problem out of the inference in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that the branch be tied.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring tying means an action is needed, which conflicts with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires no action.

steps.title: The ברייתא About Palm Branches
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute. The תנא קמא says cut palm branches must be tied before they may be used for sitting. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says tying is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: if someone cut hard palm branches for firewood and then changed his mind to use them for sitting, he must tie them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he does not need to tie them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds. This is the support for the suggestion in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The branches were first meant as firewood, so they are not a sitting item. The תנא קמא says only tying them, a real action, changes their status. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says simply deciding to use them is enough. This matches the earlier dispute between רבה and רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Hard palm branches
And he changed his mind
To tie

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Hard branches of a palm tree
that one cut for wood
and then changed his mind about them, to use them for sitting:
he must tie them.
phrases.notes: Tied before שבת, so they are not מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He does not need to tie them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not require tying, so the משנה seems to go against him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about palm branches cut for firewood.

steps.title: רב ששת: The Branch Is Still Attached to the Vine
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the משנה can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The משנה is talking about a branch that is still attached to the vine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: you can even say the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Here we are dealing with a branch that is still connected to its vine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends the משנה by saying it describes a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only said that cut wood needs no tying. The משנה is about a branch still growing on the vine, which is a different situation. So the tying requirement there has nothing to do with his rule about preparing wood.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces a defense)
What case are we dealing with here?
Still attached to its source (the vine)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not saying the branch stops being a usable item. He is only narrowing the משנה to a special case where the tying requirement comes from a different reason.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
What case are we dealing with here?
A branch still connected to its vine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 20 and 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires tying because wood needs an action, against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an attached branch, so it does not conflict with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule about cut wood.

steps.title: But You May Not Use Something Attached to the Ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. If the branch is attached, using it means using a growing plant, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he is using something attached to the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים decreed that a person may not use growing plants on שבת. A branch still on the vine is a growing plant. So how could the משנה permit drawing water with it at all?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Attached to the ground (a growing plant)

phrases.english: If so,
he is making use of something attached to the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי קָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בִּמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the branch is attached to the vine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using a growing plant is forbidden by rabbinic decree, so the משנה could not permit it.

steps.title: Below Three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The branch is attached below three טפחים from the ground, where the decree against using growing plants does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is below three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts of a plant lower than three טפחים from the ground are treated like the ground itself, similar to tree roots. The decree does not cover them. So using such a branch is allowed, and רב ששת's answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Below three טפחים (handbreadths) from the ground

phrases.english: It is below three handbreadths.
phrases.notes: There, the decree against using growing plants does not apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any attached branch is forbidden to use.
steps.terutzMaskana: A branch attached below three טפחים is outside the decree, so it may be used.

steps.title: רב אשי: A Decree That He Might Trim It
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה can even be about a cut branch. An untied branch is forbidden because of a decree that he might trim it to make it fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: you can even say it is a detached branch. It is a decree, out of concern that he might cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different defense of the משנה that does not need the 'attached branch' explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tying in the משנה is not about making wood into an item, so it does not contradict רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The worry is that with a loose branch, a person may cut and shape it on שבת to fit the pitcher, which would be a forbidden act of making a tool. A branch already tied before שבת is ready to use, so there is nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached (already cut from the plant)
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a forbidden act
In case he cuts or trims it

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to keep the משנה in line with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רב ששת says the branch is attached below three טפחים. רב אשי says it is detached, and tying is required only because of a decree that he might trim it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers show that a tying requirement does not always mean 'an action is needed to make an item usable.' Sometimes it comes from a completely different concern.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it is a detached branch;
it is a decree, in case he cuts it.
phrases.notes: He might trim and straighten it to fit the bucket.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בִּתְלוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the challenge in Steps 20 and 21, instead of רב ששת's approach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tying is required because wood needs an action to become a usable item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tying is required only because of the decree that he might trim the branch, so the משנה fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no brand-new temporary tent on יום טוב or שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the window shutter. רבי יוחנן says that all opinions agree it is forbidden to make a new temporary tent, even on יום טוב, and certainly on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's case of 'the window shutter, etc.': רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that one may not make a temporary tent from scratch on יום טוב, and it goes without saying that one may not do so on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, the window shutter. רבי יוחנן first sets down the point that everyone agrees on: making a new temporary tent is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about the window shutter. Closing a window with a shutter is like closing in a structure, much like a tent. Before explaining the argument, רבי יוחנן limits it: nobody permits building a new אהל עראי. Even on יום טוב it is forbidden, and שבת is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A window shutter or plug used to close a window opening
A temporary tent or covering, as opposed to a permanent structure
From the start, making something new
Everyone agrees (there is no dispute on this point)
And needless to say (the stricter case follows automatically)

phrases.english: 'The window shutter, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה: רבי אליעזר permits using the shutter only if it is tied and hanging; חכמים permit it either way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees that one may not make
a temporary tent from scratch on a Festival,
and needless to say, on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה (the window shutter) after finishing the discussion of the branches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree that building a new אהל עראי is forbidden on יום טוב, and all the more so on שבת.

steps.title: The dispute is only about adding to an existing tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן continues. The argument is only about adding to a tent that already exists. רבי אליעזר forbids adding even on יום טוב. חכמים permit adding even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only about adding. רבי אליעזר says: one may not add on יום טוב, and needless to say not on שבת. חכמים say: one may add on שבת, and needless to say on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his explanation by naming the one point of dispute: adding to an already-existing temporary tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a window shutter is treated like adding to an existing structure, because the house is already standing. רבי אליעזר treats even adding as forbidden building. חכמים say adding to a temporary structure is not forbidden building. This background explains why the two sides argue about the shutter in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagreed about (narrows the dispute to one point)
To add on to something that already exists
One may add (to an existing temporary tent)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the 'needless to say' direction flip. For רבי אליעזר, who forbids, the point is: if it is forbidden even on lenient יום טוב, then surely on strict שבת. For חכמים, who permit, the point is: if it is permitted even on strict שבת, then surely on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: New temporary tent: forbidden by all. Adding to an existing one: רבי אליעזר forbids and חכמים permit. This is the key to the window-shutter dispute.

phrases.english: They disagree only regarding adding.
For Rabbi Eliezer says:
One may not add on a Festival,
and needless to say, on Shabbat.
And the Rabbis say: One may add on Shabbat,
and needless to say, on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's statement. After the point everyone agrees on, it defines the exact point of dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding to an existing temporary tent: רבי אליעזר forbids it even on יום טוב, and חכמים permit it even on שבת.

steps.title: What does 'either way' mean in the חכמים's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה, 'either way one may shutter with it,' and asks what the two 'ways' are. It then begins to bring רבי אבא in the name of רב כהנא to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: 'Either way, one may shutter with it.' What does 'either way' mean? רבי אבא said in the name of רב כהנא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the wording of the חכמים in the משנה. It then sets up the answer from רבי אבא in the name of רב כהנא, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר in the משנה permits the shutter only when it is tied and hanging. So 'either way' seems to mean 'tied or not tied.' Still, the גמרא wants to know exactly which two cases the חכמים are permitting. The answer will define the scope of their leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way; both in this case and in that case
One may plug or shutter (the window)
What? (asks for the meaning of a phrase)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ פּוֹקְקִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Either way, one may shutter with it.
What is meant by 'either way'?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Kahana said:
phrases.notes: This attribution introduces the answer, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the background from רבי יוחנן, the גמרא turns to the exact wording of the חכמים's position in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which two cases does 'בין כך ובין כך' refer to in the חכמים's permission to shutter a window?
